cards.text: The LORD has a message for His people, and He speaks it through Jeremiah, His prophet. He tells them to stand at the crossroads and look, and to ask for the ancient paths: where is the good way? Then walk in it.

cards.question: The LORD promises that if they walk in the good way, they will find ___ for their souls.
True or false: The people agree to walk in the good way the LORD points them to.

cards.text: Nope. They said, “We will not walk in it!” So the LORD reminds them that He appointed watchmen over them and said, “Listen for the sound of the ram’s horn.”

cards.question: The ram’s horn is the warning signal. When the people are told to listen for it, what do they answer?

cards.text: Twice they say no. So the LORD calls out to the nations, the congregations and the whole earth to hear what will happen to this people. Friend, this just left the private chat. This went out to EVERYBODY.

cards.question: The LORD says He is bringing disaster on this people. What reason does He give?

answers.text: They ignored His word and instruction

cards.question: The LORD calls the disaster coming on this people the fruit of their own ___.

cards.text: Their gifts are fancy: frankincense from Sheba and sweet cane from a distant land, plus burnt offerings and sacrifices. I came with a price tag too, friend, and mine said 25 cents.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD says their burnt offerings are acceptable to Him.

cards.text: Therefore the LORD says He will lay stumbling blocks before this people. You know that walk across a dark living room at night, where you find every single thing you left on the floor? With your FEET?

cards.question: The LORD lays stumbling blocks before this people. Who does He say will be staggered?

cards.text: Then the LORD says to look: an army is coming from the land of the north. It's a great nation, stirred up from the ends of the earth.

cards.question: This army from the north grasps the bow and spear. How does the LORD describe them?

cards.text: Their voice roars like the sea, and they ride upon horses, lined up like men in formation against the Daughter of Zion. Friend, ONE horse lines up against me and I'm diving face-first into the chocolate chips. A whole FORMATION?

cards.question: True or false: When the people hear the report about this army, they get ready to fight.

cards.text: Instead: “We have heard the report; our hands hang limp.” Anguish grips them, pain like that of a woman in labor.

cards.question: The enemy has a sword, and terror is on every side. Where are the people told not to go?

cards.text: Stay off the road too. Then the call goes out: “O daughter of my people, dress yourselves in sackcloth and roll in ashes.”

cards.question: They're told to mourn with bitter wailing, as they would for an only son. Why mourn like that?

cards.text: Then the LORD hands out a job: “I have appointed you to examine My people like ore, so you may know and try their ways.” Mother Miller examined me once too, and decided I was worth exactly one quarter.

cards.question: After the examining, the LORD says His people are all hardened ___, walking around as slanderers.

cards.text: They are bronze and iron, and all of them are corrupt. So the fire comes: the bellows blow fiercely, blasting away the lead.

cards.question: True or false: The refining fire purges the wicked out of the people.

cards.text: The refining proceeds in vain. That's me pulling a batch out after an hour at full heat, and it's STILL dough in the middle.

cards.question: They are called rejected ___, because the ___ has rejected them.

findings.problem: "So the LORD reminds them that He appointed watchmen" adds a cause-and-effect link between the refusal in 6:16 and the watchmen in 6:17. The text doesn't make that link. Verse 17 simply begins "I appointed watchmen over you."

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: "Nope." + the quote + "So the LORD reminds them..."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story card has four sentences ("Twice they say no." / "So the LORD calls out..." / "Friend, this just left the private chat." / "This went out to EVERYBODY.").

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The right answer says they "ignored" His instruction. Jeremiah 6:19 says they paid no attention to His word and "rejected" His instruction.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "They built too many idols" has an odd tone. "Too many" implies some number of idols would be acceptable. It doesn't match the tone of the other answers.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't share the fact's core action. Verse 20 is about costly, imported offerings that are useless to the LORD. The 25-cent price tag is about being cheap, so the comparison doesn't click.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences (the stumbling blocks line, "You know that walk...?" and "With your FEET?").

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The right answer "Fathers and sons alike" stands out against two parallel "Only the..." answers. Card 11 also says the stumbling blocks are laid "before this people," which points away from the "only" options.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The second half of 6:21, "friends and neighbors will perish," never appears on any card. That detail of the passage is missing.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Stop 2's question types (MC, TF, MC, MC, FB, TF, FB) repeat stop 1's run of TF, MC, MC, FB, TF almost exactly. Stop 2 also alternates story and choice cards strictly the whole way through.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Card 1 says the army is "a great nation," which rules out the wrong answer "Small and scattered." The wrong answer "Lost and confused" isn't believable for an army grasping bow and spear.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences (the verse retelling, "Friend, ONE horse..." and "A whole FORMATION?").

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card quotes a first-person line ("We have heard the report; our hands hang limp.") without saying who is speaking. In 6:24 the speaker changes from the LORD's words to the prophet speaking with the people.

rule.text: When he quotes someone speaking as "I," he says who it is first. For example, "Then the prophet says, 'And I asked…'" (Isa 40:6).

findings.problem: "Then the call goes out: 'O daughter of my people...'" quotes a first-person speaker ("my people") without saying who it is. In 6:26 the prophet is speaking, not the LORD.

rule.text: When he quotes someone speaking as "I," he says who it is first. For example, "Then the prophet says, 'And I asked…'" (Isa 40:6).

findings.problem: The joke says Mother Miller "examined me once too, and decided I was worth exactly one quarter." In the backstory, the price sticker already said 25 cents. She picked him up and smiled; she didn't decide what he was worth. This changes his own story.

rule.text: He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: "So the fire comes" adds a cause-and-effect link between 6:28 (bronze and iron, corrupt) and 6:29 (the bellows). The text doesn't state that link.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Silver is never mentioned before this card. Earlier cards name ore, lead, bronze and iron, so "silver" and "gold" are equally reasonable for the first blank, and the baker has to guess the exact wording of 6:30.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.
